 Nirmal
 Versus

 Appearance:
 Shri Ram Narayan Dave - Advocate with Shri H.K. Vais
 Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Dilkush Kumawat - Advocate appearing on behalf   Saxena - Advocate for respondent No.3/Insurance Co.
 ORDER
With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant / claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 4.9.2008 passed in Claim Case No.302/2003 by the 21st Addl. Member Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.55,000/- has been awarded but the claims tribunal after analysing all the evidence concluded that the appellant/claimant failed to prove that accident occurred on relevant date so his application was dismissed.

entities.text: 21st Addl. Member Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Short facts of the case are that on 21.4.2000, at about 4.00 AM the appellant was going through D h a r m r a j C o l o n y , I n d o r e .
H e w a s a t h i s s i d e , a l l N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

2025:MPHC-IND:28927 2 MA-3390-2008 of a sudden, the respondent No.2/driver of the auto rickshaw bearing registration No.M.P. 09 KA 2071 (owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.3) came rashly and negligently and hit the appellant.
Resultantly, the appellant received grievous injuries on his left leg and other parts of the body.

He also got fractured on his left leg, thus rod was implanted in Verma Union Hospital, Indore where he remained hospitalized up to 30.4.2000.
4.

Earlier the appellant had filed M.A.No.2570/2004 being aggrieved by the award dated 13.8.2004 originally passed by the claims tribunal thereby rejecting the present claim petition on the same ground that there is discrepancy in the date of accident and the treatment in the Verma Union Hospital.
The said appeal ie., M.A.No.2570/2004 was allowed by this Court vide order dated Nirmal vs Girjadevi & Ors.

on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47114434/
1 4.2.2008 whereby after tentatively recording that the document shows that the appellant was treated at the Verma Hospital on 21.4.2000, had remanded the matter back to the tribunal for the reason that while dismissing the claim petition assessment of the compensation was not done which should have essentially been done for the reason that in case appeal is preferred against the award,
then appellate Court may pass appropriate order in case it is found compensation is to be awarded.
After remand the tribunal has again rejected the claim petition on the same ground that there is discrepancy in the date of accident and the treatment in the Verma Union Hospital.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant points out that the claims tribunal has remained completely oblivious of the documents which were available on NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:28927 3 MA-3390-2008 record not only of the treatment at the hospital but also relating to criminal case.
He points out by referring to those documents that consistently in all the documents, the date of accident is mentioned as 21.4.2000 and the time is mentioned as 5.45 / 6.00.
He submits that a perusal of Exhibit P/6, the MLC would show that the doctor present at the duty has wrongly recorded the date of accident and admission as 20.4.2000.
However, the time of accident is recorded as 6.00 AM and time of admission is recorded at 7.00 A.M.
In continuation he refers Exhibit P/10 the discharged card, which would show the date of admission as 21.4.2000 and the date of accident as 21.4.2000.
The date of discharge is shown as 30.4.2000.
He then refers to Exhibit P/33, the 'admission form' which provides the date of admission as 21.4.2000 and time of admission 7.00 and the date of discharge is 30.4.2000.

He thus submits that even if the documents only in respect of treatment at Verma Hospital are seen then also it is clearly established that accident occurred on 21.4.2000 and the injured was admitted on 21.4.2000 itself and not on 20.4.2000.
A mere mistake in MLC would not render the entire claim of the petition as unbelievable.
He further refers to Exhibit P/1, which is First Information Report registered at Crime No.120/24.4.2000 in which also the date of accident is mentioned as 21.4.2000 and time as 5.45.
Same is the case with other documents relating to criminal case.

He thus points out that the claims tribunal has completely erred in not believing the claimant and rejecting the claim merely on the basis of one instance of discrepancy that too for the mistake of the treating doctor who instead of 21.4.2000 has mentioned 20.4.2000 as the date of admission which has no consequences at NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28927 4 MA-3390-2008 all looking to all other consistent documents which were available on the record in abundance.
He further points out that the appellant remained admitted for a period of ten days and suffered fracture in shaft of femur bone of left leg and also rod was inserted in the same.
6. He further submits that the claims tribunal has also recorded a finding in para 6 of the impugned award that the driver of the insured vehicle was not having valid license.

Thus it was being operated in the breach of the insurance policy hence the Insurance Company is not liable for payment of compensation even if the appellant is found entitled for payment of compensation.

He submits that this finding of the claims tribunal has now required to be overturned in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in light of Bajaj Allianz General Ins. Co. Ltd V/s. Rambha Devi & Others,
reported as 2024 ACJ 2623 .

Vaijanti & Others reported as 1995 ACJ 560 and points out that in criminal proceedings strict principle of proof like criminal case is not required.

Transport Corporation & Anr . reported as AIR 2019 SC 994 for the said proposition.
Thus he prays for appropriate enhancement of compensation.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 / Insurance Co. submits that the claim of the appellant has been dismissed twice by two different claims tribunal.
Thus no interference in the findings of fact recorded by the tribunal is warranted.

He submits that in MLC Exhibit P/6 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28927 5 MA-3390-2008 and X-ray Exhibit P/5, it has been clearly recorded that the accident occurred on 20.4.2000 and as per FIR the date of accident is 21.4.2000 hence there is clear discrepancy for which the claim is liable to be rejected hence no interference is warranted in the award.

entities.text: MLC Exhibit P/6 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He also points out that even the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid license.
Thus the Insurance Co. cannot be made liable to pay compensation in case Court finds entitlement of the appellant to get compensation.

He also submits that the matter is pending since last 25 years and in case the compensation is awarded then also Insurance Co. does not deserve to be saddled with liability of payment of insurance for such a long period because it is not at fault for pendency of the appeal.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.
The claims tribunal while considering the evidence available on record has acted in most casual manner.
It has placed heavy reliance on Exhibit P/6 the MLC report and Exhibit P/5 the X-ray plate.
Both of these documents were written by same doctor.

However, the witness who came to be examined by the claimant in support of his claim before the tribunal, the employee / record keeper of the Verma Union Hospital (PW.2) has not only clearly proved the documents regarding treatment of the appellant but had also clarified that the appellant was admitted in the hospital on 21.4.2000 at 7.00 A.M.
The claims tribunal while considering the timings has unnecessarily referred to the timing of admission as 2.00 P.M. which is not to be found in any of the documents regarding treatment.

Even Exhibit P/6 the MLC report provides that the accident occurred at 6.00 A.M and patient NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28927 6 MA-3390-2008 was admitted at 7.00 A.M. Exhibit P/10 the discharged card summerizes the date of admission and discharged which provides that the patient was admitted on 21.4.2000 and discharged on 30.4.2000.
Not only this even the admission form Exhibit P/33 provides that the appellant was admitted on 21.4.2000.

All the consistent documents if read in juxtaposition of the documents in criminal case for example Exhibit P/1 the FIR then it also establishes that the accident has occurred on 21.4.2000 at around 5.45 A.M. Thus in the considered view of this Court, there is clear consistency in the evidence which is available on record hence clearly the tribunal has erred in rejecting the claim on this ground.
As regards the liability of the Insurance Co. the tribunal itself has recorded in para 6 of the impugned award that the driver of the auto rickshaw was having LMV license.
In view of the law as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Rambha Devi & Others (supra), a person holding LMV license can very well drive the auto rickshaw.
Thus the finding as contained in para 6 is also not sustainable in the eyes of law.

Consequently, the appellant is hereby held entitled for compensation as he has sufficiently proved the occurrence of accident on 21.4.2000 so also the diagnosis of fracture in shaft femur bone of left leg having operation closed interlocking intramedullary nailing with proximal end dirtel locking as well as the bills incurred by him on his treatment.
As regards the quantum of compensation the tribunal has assessed the amount of compensation at Rs.55,000/-.
Considering Nirmal vs Girjadevi & Ors.

on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47114434/
3 the long pendency of the appeal, this Court is of the considered view that the compensation as a lump sum should be quantified as Rs.80,000/- which would constitute a just and proper NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28927 7 MA-3390-2008 compensation.
The enhanced amount of Rs.80,000/- shall carry the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition.
10. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
